metric.definition: Order-to-delivery time for transformers, switchgear, generators, cooling plant, and high-end accelerators.

reading.body:
Critical equipment lead times for transformers, switchgear, generators, cooling plant, and high-end accelerators have stretched from months to years, making them as binding on data center construction as permits.

The pattern is a shift in the supply chain from a routine procurement step to a schedule gate. Electrical and cooling equipment that once arrived in months now determines when a building can be energized and commissioned, so the supply chain sets the timeline as firmly as permitting does.

For AI, this matters because data centers are the physical layer of compute. If these components take years to arrive, new compute capacity cannot come online on schedule, which directly constrains how fast AI workloads can scale.

The data does not provide specific lead times, regional differences, or vendor-level detail. It also does not show whether lead times are still lengthening or beginning to shorten, only that they have moved from months to years and now gate construction schedules.
